The submission is frozen. Final report:

## Frozen predictor (submission.py, pure stdlib, stateless)

`mean = −1.8159 + 1.0487·CURVE[elapsed+15] − 0.006·(mass − 74) + 0.005·(recent HR − 165)`

- **CURVE** is the 5‑minute‑smoothed, cross‑person *median* core temperature versus elapsed exercise minute (1…60) computed from the 14 labelled training people (37.36 °C at minute 1 → ≈38.67 °C plateau after ~50 min). The target time is `elapsed + horizon` (clamped to 1–60); `elapsed` is `time_min[last] − time_min[first] + 1` with a fallback to `len(history)`, so it is invariant to clock shifts (verified: random offsets of ±1000 min change nothing).
- **Mass** term (first non‑null mass; default 74 kg) and **HR** term (mean of last ≤3 non‑null HR values; zero adjustment when HR is missing, as in the first 5 minutes).
- **Interval**: symmetric half‑width `0.65 + 0.005·max(0, tt−19)`, clipped to [0.6, 1.0] → width 1.3–1.7 °C (always within the 0 < width ≤ 5 rule). Output clamped to 36.0–40.5 °C. No identity features, no absolute time.

## Development evidence (dev_score, 84 requests, 4 people)
| version | person‑balanced MAE | per‑person MAE | coverage90 | interval score |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| template (ECTemp‑style) | 0.539 | H08 .65, H17 .15, H20 .73, H24 .63 | 0.44 | 3.60 |
| curve + mass (ridge fit) | 0.321 | .07 / .95 / .06 / .20 | 0.74 | 4.04 |
| curve + mass + HR(0.005), ±0.6 | 0.307 | .07 / .95 / .07 / .13 | 0.74 | 3.65 |
| **final** (mass −0.006, HR 0.005, growing interval) | **0.290** | .07 / .92 / .04 / .13 | 0.79 | 2.87 |

Hot‑subset (40 requests) person‑balanced MAE of the final model: 0.052.

## Training‑side evidence
Only 9 of 14 training people have a watts decrease (190 "3A‑type" origins), so I built 584 origin rows (every origin t≥4, horizon 15) from all 14 people and used leave‑one‑person‑out CV, scoring both all rows and 3A‑type rows. Constant/time‑curve alone: ≈0.245 person‑balanced MAE; adding mass: ≈0.22; HR with a fixed small slope (0.003–0.005 °C/bpm, full‑data fit 0.004) was neutral on 3A rows and helpful on all rows (0.253→0.239); slopes ≥0.01 hurt. Skin temperature, skin slope, HR drift, W/kg, ambient, humidity, age, height, BMI did not improve LOPO error and were dropped. Final fixed‑coefficient model: LOPO person‑balanced MAE 0.226 (all rows), residual 5/95 % quantiles ≈ −0.42/+0.53 °C.

## Causal inputs used
Elapsed time from the history (not absolute time_min), body mass, the last ≤3 heart‑rate values. Skin temperature, watts, ambient and humidity are read but not used (no robust LOPO benefit with this sample size).

## Uncertainty and limitations
- The forecast is essentially a population time‑curve with small covariate corrections; the residual is dominated by the unobservable person‑level core‑temperature offset. Dev person H17 (light, young, low wattage) ran ≈0.9 °C below the population curve with nothing in its inputs flagging it, which caps the achievable MAE and is why the interval was widened (train LOPO coverage at the final width ≈99 %, dev 79 %). On hidden people, coverage will likely fall short of 90 % whenever such low/high responders occur.
- Coefficients were estimated on 14 people (mass sign is supported by train but contradicted by one dev person; it was shrunk from −0.008 to −0.006 as a hedge). HR effect is small and physiologically plausible but weakly identified.
- The curve is only defined for elapsed+15 ≤ 60 min; longer sessions reuse the plateau value. Histories must start near exercise onset for the elapsed‑time curve to be meaningful; the dev requests all do.
- The 3B branch is not specially handled (variant 3A was the target); if called it returns the curve value at `elapsed + horizon_min` (horizon 0).
